End-to-end routes: issuance, arbitrage and settlement
29 September 2026. Conditional route classification for the pDAI thesis. Diagrams describe obligations
and asset flows, not instructions to alter live contracts. Historical observations and hypothetical
integrations are separated.
Scope and common test
There is no finite list of every possible future protocol or strategy. This atlas covers the accounting
families in the maintained bridge, wrapper and liquidity inventory. A particular route is complete only
when it identifies:
Source asset, execution environment, issuance rule and legitimate authority.
Receipt and destination token addresses, unit conversions and exact custody.
Message verification, timing, destination permission and capacity.
Funded output at every exchange or financing step.
The closing asset, all debt/settlement obligations and remaining inventory.
Net profit for each participant and the consolidated system, separately.
The effect on executable pDAI buying and selling at the stated size.
An arrow is conditional on these checks. Funding a pDAI position is not itself arbitrage: retaining pDAI
leaves price exposure. A closed arbitrage cycle returns the starting asset with a surplus after costs and
restores borrowed principal and collateral as specified. Market making may earn income over time
without being risk-free or ending each transaction with restored inventory.

Issuance authority before any route
The strongest theoretical scenario can grant arbitrary source balances and relevant governance
permissions. Even then, destination acceptance, message rules and output funding remain separate
premises. An accepted accounting balance can fund a finite trade without establishing sound backing.
Neither this assumption nor a copied L1 contract proves a functioning source L2. Historical baseline
(Appendix 13), cross-chain comparison (Appendix 7).

1. Ordinary escrow return
An empty escrow blocks the release unless that exact integration has an additional authorized source of
tokens. Validator control does not turn a transfer call into minting. The audited standard gateway
selections for OUSD, mUSD, eUSD and FRAX are not proof of native-source reverse minting of those
existing tokens. Their individual destination issuer paths are separate. Issuance inventory (Appendix 4).

2. Native-source custody and reverse representation
This mobilizes a claim while its underlying investment stays in place. The purchaser, not the original
depositor, now owns that exclusive represented claim. Outright sale needs no repayment by the seller
but transfers an asset; its proceeds are not automatically income. Reverse ARB is a historical
architectural example, not proof that every stablecoin recognizes the same representation. Bridge
models (Appendix 13).

3. Token-specific burn/mint or shortfall issuance
Destination ARB and GRT mint observations establish particular mechanisms; GRT's allowed escrow
shortfall and ARB's reverse custody have different source accounting. Do not infer universal mint
authority from either. LPT has a source-level shortfall branch, while the observed LPT withdrawal used
escrow. Specialized history (Appendix 20), GRT reconciliation (Appendix 12).

4. Aave Portal: local advance with settlement
Issuing M and recovering Q local underlying settles from those proceeds alone only when Q ≥ M + F, with
settlement fee F. Ordinary loan repayment does not cancel the same unbacked balance. The audited
stablecoin unbacked caps were zero. Historical local modified-fork experiments do not establish a public
source-to-destination Portal cycle. Portal ledger (Appendix 17).

5. Relayer or inventory bridge
Relayer income is a fee for funding, execution and settlement risk. It is not new destination principal.
Across is the studied example; a Frax-specific bridge/Ferry route would require its own deployed identity
and settlement proof, not merely the shared label of a bridge. Bridge revenue can finance support only
to the extent controlled, collected and not committed elsewhere. Across comparison (Appendix 7), 
HubPool accounting (Appendix 14).

6. Collateralized lending or local issuance
Fraxlend is an asset/collateral pair, while authorized FRAX AMO issuance is a separate capability. Reserve
issuance requires the exact basket assets and usable conditions; a registered symbol is insufficient.
Origin, mUSD and other issuer candidates need their own compatible collateral and redemption
accounts. Borrowing to hold pDAI is a funded position, not a completed profitable cycle. Reserve
inventory (Appendix 18), Frax/Convex study (Appendix 47).

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 340

7. Local market paths and nested lending receipts
This includes direct pDAI/PLS trades, stablecoin triangulation, FRAX/3CRV underlying routes, other
metapools, and Curve/Balancer discrepancies. Each additional pool, rate conversion and withdrawal
needs an executable quote. Wrapped-to-main swaps consume main-token capacity. Moving the same
asset through more wrappers does not multiply its reserves. Wrapper inventory (Appendix 24), Pool
accounting (Appendix 16).
For the illustrative graph with FRAX, pUSDC, pDAI and PLS and its five named pools, the three simple
cycles through PLS are:
PLS → pDAI → pUSDC → PLS
PLS → FRAX → pUSDC → PLS
PLS → pDAI → pUSDC → FRAX → PLS
Each has a reverse orientation. T wo-leg reversal in one pool is a separate fee-losing round trip. This
enumerates topology, not profitable execution. Repeated or combined walks change state, share
reserves and may impose gas, credit and timing costs; they cannot be valued by adding independent
initial quotes. The cycle experiment (Appendix 47) tests selected sizes and states, not all strategies in
every possible deployment.

8. LP , lending and reward income
This is productive deployment and possible income, not necessarily arbitrage. Reward bridging does not
transport interchangeable LP principal. A share in future interest is not presently withdrawable
underlying. Each asset belongs in one consolidated account with its associated claims and obligations.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 342

Large sales: complete local correction
This closes the trader's account. It does not close the treasury's remaining pDAI exposure. A standing bid
is one proposed explicit closing venue, not a historically established redemption facility. Without it, the
complete alternate market route must supply equivalent funded demand. Source funding arriving after
the seller needs payment cannot finance that earlier payment without an advance or existing buffer.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 343

Large purchases: complete local correction
Available pDAI can come from retained inventory, a funded third-party sale, a permitted withdrawal of
owned claims, an escrow release with inventory, or an exact-token issuance route that actually exists.
Borrowing pDAI adds a later return obligation. Minting an unrelated stablecoin is not another branch for
minting pDAI. Purchases return system-held pDAI to outside buyers, so accumulation need not be
monotonic.
What L2 participation can earn
A source-chain operator earns only the revenue attached to its actual role: issuance revenue if any after
obligations, lending income after funding and losses, bridge/relayer fees after reimbursement, owned LP
income, or its own closed trading profit. An external arbitrageur's profit is not automatically L2 or
treasury revenue. If the same system owns both sides, consolidate them; internal payments disappear
and remaining asset, liability and outside-cash changes determine the result.
The route diagrams are composable. Every connection remains conditional on its own finite capacity,
and mechanisms drawing on the same reserve are not independent sources of funding. Adding a future
protocol requires adding its specific edge and settlement rules, not declaring the atlas universally
complete.
